entries.1.64:
[RC6] Fixed Nexerelin Random mode crash.
[RC5]
  - Nemean Lion system now behaves properly under AI control.
  - Acheron's generation tweaked so that there is no longer so much empty space with the next procgen system.
  - Miniguns no longer listed as benefitting from energy modifiers (they still do, but the mount type shenanigans broke the refit screen).
  - Hopefully plugged the last memory leak from Scy.
  - Added Civilian and fake Militarized Subsystems hullmods built-in to all civies, as a horribly convoluted workaround to the skill thresholds issue.

Singularity Torpedo:
   . Removed from all variants and from Scy's available blueprints.
   . It is now only available from rare salvage, and will probably be moved to Seeker/TaDA at some point along the Light Plating, Reactive Armor and Economical Maintenance hullmods.

BALANCING:

  - Phased Missile Launcher: Ammo increased to 15 from 12.

  - Cluster Torpedo Launcher: Ammo increased to 10 from 6.

  - Arc Missile:
   . Hp raised to 400 from 200,
   . Damage stats messed with (but not the arcs),
   . Rack OP cost lowered to 3 from 4.

  - KAcc mk.1:
   . Damage per shot reduced to 150 from 160,
   . DPS increased to 150 from 140,
   . Flux to fire reduced to 165 from 173.
   . Overall slightly more efficient with a cleaner stat card, fits better as a third alternative between the Railgun and LDA.

  - KAcc mk.2:
   . Flux to fire reduced to 480 from 500,
   . Now fires in bursts of 2 rounds.
   . A smidgen more flux efficient, half the burst damage of the Heavy Needler, but a decent armor pen and causes very long overloads.

  - KAcc mk.3: DPS increased to 333 Kinetic dmg/s from 300.

  - HEMor mk.1: Flux to fire reduced to 210 from 235.

  - HEMor mk.2: Flux to fire reduced to 600 from 700.

  - Light Energy Blaster: Flux to fire reduced to 360 from 400.

  - Most PD weapons received the NO_TURN_BOOST_WHILE_IDLE tag with adjusted turn rates.

  - Balius-class freighter: Cargo capacity increased to 350 from 250.

  - Balius-class tanker: Fuel capacity increased to 600 from 500.

BUGFIXES/IMPROVEMENTS:

  - Fixed *many* memory leaks. (Can't say how significant they were, but every bit helps I suppose)
  - Slight code optimization.
  - Fixed some typos here and there.
  - Cross-mods compatibilities updated.
  - Every single weapon was redrawn to ensure they are displayed sharp in the game. Lots of reworked muzzle and glow effects.

entries.v1.3: 9/24/2023 - Added the Valkyrie (H) and the Colossus Mk.III (H). The Mudskipper (A) lost its ground support hullmod, as the Valkyrie (H) now fulfills the role of dedicated troop transport. The old Colossus Mk.III has been converted into the Colossus (A), a dedicated freighter. A partial patch for Iron Shell (0.96 compatible version of Iron Shell available on the Unofficial Starsector Chat Discord) has been added, allowing the Iron Shell to use some of the new vessels. The Mule (A) received a small OP nerf, the Condor (H) received a second variant, and all variant files received a balance patch to hopefully make them more effective and less likely to default to going over their OP limits. NOTE: This update is NOT savefile compatible with v1.2b or lower.

Also tweaked the default ship roles and Hegemony faction files to, once again, make the Shepherd (A) spawn properly in Hegemony fleets.

summary.paragraph: Adds 14 pilotable strikecrafts, 2 new fighter wings, and 3 corvettes that bridge the gap between strikecraft and frigates. Includes an optional submod adding 2 pilotable variants of Kadur-Mayasuran strikecraft. Requires Mayasuran Navy and Arma Armatura.

summary.paragraph: Adds 2 pilotable variants of Kadur-Mayasuran strikecraft. This is an optional submod for Mayasuran Fighter Expansion.

summary.sentence: Adds a missions mod with an arcade-style coin-operated theme.
summary.paragraph: Introduces a missions mod designed as a community experiment with an arcade aesthetic. It currently includes a level called Cow Purge and aims to collect various arcadey ideas for modders to build upon.

summary.sentence: Adds interstellar gladiator battles that can be accessed through a com relay.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to subscribe to a gladiator program to participate in matches broadcast across the sector. Offers unique bounties and an endless battle mode for end-game content. Includes special ships and fleets, and provides a framework for other mods to add their own gladiators and bounties.

summary.sentence: Makes building in cheaper hullmods viable by adding a portion of the OP difference to the hull.
summary.paragraph: When building in a cheaper hullmod, the mod calculates the OP difference and adds a percentage of it to the hull. Using Better Deserved S Mods or Progressive S Mods reduces this effectiveness, and using both nullifies the mod. The ratios and base bonus multipliers are adjustable in the settings file.

summary.sentence: Allows players to replace the default portrait with a custom image to play as themselves.
summary.paragraph: Replaces the placeholder portrait image with a user-provided picture. Requires the user to prepare a 128x128px PNG file and place it in the mod's graphics folder.

summary.sentence: Reduces weapon and combat ship availability while making NPC colonies stronger.
summary.paragraph: This minimod makes several changes to the campaign layer. Weapons and combat ships become scarce and highly regulated, with only Military and Black Markets selling higher tier items. All ships are d-modded, and accessing Black Markets requires using a fence. Factions are heavily armed, and actions have broader reputation consequences.

summary.paragraph: Introduces a new playable faction centered around advanced android technology. The mod includes custom ship designs, portraits, and planet art to support the narrative of a rogue AI seeking survival. It requires LazyLib to function properly.

summary.sentence: Adds a series of quests that unlock instantaneous travel between a limited number of gates.
summary.paragraph: Adds a short series of quests that open up instantaneous travel between Gates and are intended to feel like a natural extension to the vanilla game. Once activated, the player may travel to any other active Gate for a fuel cost based on the distance traveled. The mod encourages early exploration and eases later-game traveling without feeling like a cheat.

summary.sentence: Adds a small selection of hullmods that can be used to filter weapons based on certain characteristics.
summary.paragraph: Adds a small selection of hullmods that can be used to filter weapons based on certain characteristics. Current filters include damage type, range, PD/Non-PD, and beam/projectile. The mod requires lazylib.

summary.sentence: Changes package behavior to grant single blueprints for each item instead of unlocking them.
summary.paragraph: This mod alters how packages function by providing a single blueprint for every item contained within, rather than unlocking the items themselves. By default, it affects only vanilla packages, though mod-added packages can be adjusted manually via their associated scripts.

summary.sentence: Provides a utility for modders to visualize AI flags and ship targeting data during gameplay.
summary.paragraph: Displays visual indicators for maneuver targets, ship targets, and mouse positions using colored diamonds. Shows active AI flags and their custom data on-screen, with floating text updates when flags change state. Includes a console command to force AI flags for testing purposes.

summary.sentence: Adds more than a hundred lore-friendly portraits to the game for use by the player and other factions.
summary.paragraph: Adds more than a hundred lore-friendly portraits to the game. These portraits are available at the start of the campaign to the player and are also used by other factions. The installation process is the same as for other mods.

summary.paragraph: This mod introduces a massive expansion including new factions like the Sidus Dim and Caelus Defense Force, along with hundreds of new ships and weapons. It features new campaign missions, phase mechanics, and custom music. Players can engage in new scenarios such as attacking independent convoys or defending against strike forces.

summary.sentence: Increases the maximum player level to 103 and reduces the experience required to level up after level 35.
summary.paragraph: This mod adjusts the experience requirement formula to make leveling up less tedious at high levels. It raises the cap to 103, which is necessary to unlock all skills, and gradually lowers the XP needed per level starting from level 36. The change is negligible at lower levels but reduces the requirement for level 103 by approximately 90% compared to the vanilla formula.

summary.sentence: Adds a secretive organization that sells dossiers with locations and scanning frequencies for hidden post-Collapse sites containing blueprints.
summary.paragraph: Provides a repeatable way to find more blueprints by purchasing access to hidden sites as they appear. The mod includes hidden dangers at these locations and filters out certain unwanted drops like derelicts. It is designed to be lore-friendly and compatible with other major mods like Nexerelin.

summary.sentence: Adds missions, exploration, unique ships, and scripted encounters to liven up the sector.
summary.paragraph: Introduces quests and exploration featuring many unique ships and scripted encounters. Includes Anomalies, which are artificial constructions of unknown origin, and Artifacts, which are man-made products of Domain technology. Gameplay features events influenced by the player, hidden systems to explore, and consequences for actions.

summary.sentence: Provides economy services to check shortages, surpluses, and price extremes for any commodity.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to track commodity shortages, surpluses, and high or low prices. This information can also be monitored through side intel within the game.

summary.sentence: Allows browsing player storage and transferring cargo and ships to a master storage or via courier services.
summary.paragraph: Provides convenient browsing of player storage content to quickly locate cargo and ships. Players can define a master storage for regular transfers of all cargo and ships from other storages, or request courier services while traveling. Any transfer incurs a fee based on distance, collected at the end of the month.

summary.sentence: Provides a sector-wide hyperspace network to query market content, search for personnel with specific personalities, and locate ships for sale.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to search for administrators or officers with a given personality, query markets for weapons, fighter wings, modspecs, or blueprints, and locate specific ships for sale. It serves as an information services tool for the game.

summary.sentence: Adds a production-based mini-mod that allows scanning and building weapons, fighter LPCs, and ships using resources and cores.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to analyze weapons, LPCs, and ships by consuming cores to unlock them for future production. Enables the construction of weapons, fighter LPCs, and ships by purchasing them in the market screen, consuming resources like metal, rare metal, and fuel. Also includes an option to order ships from sector markets at a premium markup.

summary.paragraph: Players can purchase station contracts to build facilities on planets, construct various buildings, and set up to three fleet configurations. These fleets spawn automatically to perform tasks such as trading, mining, or patrolling, with specific contracts available for different factions.

summary.sentence: Replaces vanilla starting ship options with an interactive narrative offering varied ship, financial, and faction choices.
summary.paragraph: Provides a wider selection of starting ships for new campaigns through an interactive narrative structure. Offers three distinct trees of options for flagship, support, and logistics vessels. Balances choices so that player preference and role-playing determine the best starting scenario rather than a single optimal path.

summary.sentence: Adds 126 pieces of space-themed music totaling over 7.5 hours to increase immersion.
summary.paragraph: Adds a collection of space orchestra, ambient, and instrumental tracks with light chorus vocals. The music is designed to be immersive, avoiding genres like rap, metal, pop, dub-step, and jazz. It replaces the original repetitive Starsector music tracks for title, campaign, and battle sequences.

summary.sentence: Adds a new universally hostile faction with custom ships, weapons, and a mobile fleet base called the Oasis.
summary.paragraph: Introduces The Nomads faction, which travels around the sector in the Oasis. The faction is hostile to most groups but neutral to the player and other independent factions. If the Oasis is destroyed, its escort fleets scatter, and the station becomes available for purchase. The mod also includes demo missions and optional support for GraphicsLib and Nexerelin.

summary.sentence: Provides easier early-game access to military ships and insurance coverage for losses.
summary.paragraph: Offers a special store with discounted ships for beginners and insurance that covers ship losses. The store is accessible at lower levels, and insurance payouts taper off as the player's level increases. Contributions from veterans help fund these services for new starfarers.

summary.sentence: Replaces Vanilla AI systems with a faster, feature-complete alternative that improves performance in large battles.
summary.paragraph: Provides a common framework and well-documented codebase for developing new AIs. Supports auto-fire weapons, most missiles, drones, and all Vanilla systems while optimizing performance. Includes features like hull ID blacklisting and is designed to be future-proof for modders.

summary.sentence: Adds individual blueprints for ships, weapons, and fighters that are part of a blueprint package but lack their own rare drop, making them easier to acquire.
summary.paragraph: This mod provides common blueprints for all ships, weapons, and fighters included in a blueprint package that do not have a rare drop variant. These blueprints are significantly easier to obtain than rare drops, allowing factions to specialize in specific ship types more readily.

summary.paragraph: Adds a custom faction featuring infected-themed ships, weapons, and hullmods. Includes campaign integration, custom missions, and various ship systems. Ships are largely based on vanilla sprites with custom details and placements.

summary.sentence: Replaces default weapon effects with faster, lower-particle special effects that utilize multiple cores.
summary.paragraph: Replaces the default Starsector weapon effects with cheaper, faster-rendering special effects that look better than Vanilla's glows and smoke. The system is considerably faster because it uses few particles and multiple cores for math. It provides extensive support for modders to easily add new effects with properties like color shifts and rotational effects.

summary.sentence: Adds a faction of mysterious, uncrewed warships with unique combat systems that trade mobility for firepower and resilience.
summary.paragraph: Introduces numerous ships, fighters, and weapons inspired by WWII naval vessels, featuring custom mechanics like the Phoenix Hull Composition and Flux Sink systems. These systems allow ships to tank damage and generate power for massive offensive bursts, creating a playstyle focused on broadside gunplay and flux management. The mod includes a demo version with missions and a variety of ship classes ranging from interceptors to battleline cruisers.

summary.sentence: Adds an option to automatically activate the transponder when jumping into friendly systems and optionally deactivate it when jumping to hyperspace.
summary.paragraph: This mini-mod provides a setting for jump points leading to friendly systems that activates your transponder during the jump. It also offers an optional feature to deactivate the transponder when entering hyperspace, which can be disabled if the user prefers to keep it on. The mod prompts the user if the destination system contains a market that is not hostile and belongs to a faction whose patrols conduct transponder checks.

summary.sentence: Adds Mass Effect-themed ships and missions to Starfarer, including the SSV Normandy SR1 and the Collector Ship.
summary.paragraph: Introduces a campaign featuring the SSV Normandy SR1 versus the Collector Ship, allowing players to use the Normandy. Includes missions and campaign starting conditions based on the Mass Effect universe, though currently uses vanilla weapons.

summary.sentence: Replaces original factions with four major and three minor ones, adds over 100 unique ships and weapons, and introduces a randomly generated campaign map with new gameplay systems like mining, salvage, and ship requisition.
summary.paragraph: Replaces the original Starsector factions with four major powers and several minor groups, each with unique ship and weapon technologies. Adds a completely randomly generated campaign map with over 100 stars and introduces new gameplay mechanics including asteroid mining, salvage operations, planetary surveys, and direct ship requisition from faction shipyards. Players can choose from five different starting careers that impact their initial resources, relationships, and available options.

summary.paragraph: Adds several new factions, tons of ships and weapons. Includes custom music, portraits, and interaction images. Features a total conversion background lore involving a lost colony fleet.

summary.sentence: Allows players to salvage Derelict and Remnant AI ships in battle.
summary.paragraph: This mod enables the salvage of Derelict and Remnant AI vessels, removing built-in D-mods from Derelicts and lowering the maintenance profile for the Rampart-class cruiser. While Derelicts remain generally weak, Remnant ships are useful as they do not require crew and feature numerous Synergy mounts, though the mod may conflict with other modifications affecting AI ships.

summary.sentence: Adds two highly advanced, science-worshipping factions, the Looters and the Noir, along with their unique ships and weapons.
summary.paragraph: Introduces a race hidden in a thick nebula that split into two factions: the Looters, who act as pirates to recover raw materials, and the Noir, who spread their religion-based science. Both factions share the same technology and are led by the same council. The mod includes new sprites for weapons and ships, as well as campaign faction interactions.

summary.sentence: Fixes the "empty planets" bug in systems from The Core Worlds by generating Planetary Conditions using the same logic Starsector normally uses.
summary.paragraph: On first load, the mod finds all empty planets and generates Planetary Conditions for them. It fixes empty Planetary Conditions, changes the Hazard Rating from the default 100%, and makes these planets provide Survey Data normally. It also prints a summary on the screen when done.

summary.sentence: Adds a total conversion featuring the Lemurian Empire, Thiian Confederation, and Esk Coalition fighting the cybernetic Terran Dominion in a three-way war.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to take control of the Lemurian Fleet as an immortal admiral to fight for survival against the Terran Dominion. The mod includes three major playable factions with distinct ship designs and gameplay styles, along with minor factions like the Ershiian Sovereignty. It features new mechanics such as boarding hostile stations for resources and a narrative set in the Sovereign System.

summary.sentence: Adds a new pirate faction with 17 ship designs, 5 weapons, a new planet, and larger fleet battles.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Lotus Conglomerate faction, starting as neutral to the player. Includes a new planet in the Corvus system with a contraband station, a showcase mission, and numerous new ships and weapons. Increases fleet sizes in campaigns and missions.

entries.0.8.3:
+Exerelin's Corvus mode compatible! Don't forget to change Nexerelin's mod_info (you'll see what to change).
+2 new random missions from MesoTroniK. Thanks!
+2 new Rip Drive system variants, light and heavy. Both have less charges, more cooldown and less time.
+New hull explosion sounds! CH-BOOOM! KRK-POW!
-Engine style changes. Now smokey instead of glowing!
-Ship balancing: Torus is more tanky, less offensively capable. Driver's flux stats boosted. Tacit buffed.
   -Many other changes in many fields. It's irresponsible of me to not document them. >.>
-Sound updates: Most medium/small weapons have new sounds as well as the Concussion Beam and Zeus.
-Sprite Updates: Porter-class and Ayre class.
-Significantly buffed Plasma Blasters. Now, they deal good damage and taper out as they fire for longer.
-Changed Meteor and Striker. Larger volleys, faster speed but a slow reload. Also improved graphics.
-Removed the Cobra's ammo mechanic. Not fun enough.
-Nerfed K-Barrage by decreasing its accuracy limit and increasing its accuracy loss rate. Also nerfed ammo.
-Nerfed Parabola's range from 6000 to 2000. Effectively an MRM, but still able to go very far (with inertia).
-Buffed Heavy eFlak. It now features a larger blast radius.
-Buffed Plasma Launcher on the Conduit with a larger blast radius. Still iffy on this one.

summary.sentence: Adds a new mercenary corporation with 17 ships and 26 unique weapons focused on mobility and specialized roles.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Citadel, a new faction offering ships that prioritize speed and flux management over hull and armor. The mod includes a wide variety of new weapons designed to fill specific combat niches, along with new ships, fighters, and system interactions.

extras.license: All assets from this project may be used without obtaining explicit permission as long as... No laws are broken and Fractal Softworks' terms of service are not violated The original authors of any assets used are credited The assets are not used for nefarious purposes
extras.saveCompatibility: Yes, adding ICE to a game later on will enable all of it's features. This hasn't been tested extensively however, so create a backup of your save file first. Also be aware that the economy of the markets this mod adds will take a while to stabilize.

summary.sentence: Adds a new faction with 17 ships, 18 weapons, 7 ship systems, 7 hull mods, and phase cloak technology.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Idoneus Citadel Exiles, a faction featuring ships with powerful armor repair and evasion but no shields. Includes new weapons like the Nosferatu Fusor and Mine Pod, along with hull mods such as the Recall Teleporter. The faction has two markets located at the Idoneus Citadel station and the Exiled Idoneus Colony Fleet.

entries.0.6.1: Added the "Direct Retreat" hullmod which changes the automatic retreat type (for ships with one of the retreat hullmods) from a standard defensive retreat to the "get the hell out of here" direct retreat.
entries.0.6.0: Added hullmods to change the personality of a ship (ships default to Steady in vanilla). Doesn't work on ships with officers or the flagship.
entries.0.5.1:
Updated Version Checker support
Fixed the bug where removing non-AS hullmods would cause the hull- and cr-related AS hullmods to also be removed.

summary.sentence: Adds hullmods that allow the player to set predefined battle commands for AI-piloted ships in their fleet.
summary.paragraph: These hullmods cost 0 ordnance points and enable behaviors such as automatic retreat based on hull integrity, missile count, peak performance time, or CR level. They also allow changing the personality of ships without officers to be more or less aggressive. The mod includes a direct retreat option and supports version checking.

summary.sentence: Adds a fleet of robotic warships with quick shields, high flux dissipation, and powerful weaponry suited for hit-and-run tactics.
summary.paragraph: Adds a fleet of robotic warships that feature quick shields, high flux dissipation, and high flux/power weaponry, making them more suited for hit-and-run tactics than frontal attacks. Many of these ships are bumped up technological tiers compared to vanilla human ship designs. Most ships feature multitudes of light HELR Burst Beam Projectors that function in defensive and offensive applications.

summary.sentence: Implements cleanup functions for scavenger fleets and debris fields to improve performance in the mid/late game.
summary.paragraph: Automatically cleans up scavenger fleets stuck trying to return to their home planet when the player docks at a planet or station. Ensures debris fields expire properly. This is a standalone mod that works alongside Nexerelin or DynaSector.

summary.sentence: Adds a variety of new ships, including capitals, cruisers, frigates, and wings, to the game.
summary.paragraph: Introduces numerous new vessels ranging from vanilla-friendly designs to powerful, game-breaking options like the Omega dreadnought. Players can find these ships in participating shipyards or test them in local simulators. The mod includes updated missions and rebalanced variants alongside the new content.

summary.sentence: Adds a new high-tech faction with 24 ships, 11 weapons, and basic ship systems focused on drone and energy weapon combat.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Arkandian Institute faction, which is high-tech and relies heavily on drone systems and energy weapons while lacking missile capability. The mod includes 24 new ships, mostly frigates, along with 11 new weapons and a couple of basic ship systems. The faction is located in the Arkan system within the core worlds and has established small outposts in neighboring systems.

The mod introduces 34 new ships across various classes, 8 new weapons, and the Singula star system where the conflict unfolds. It includes detailed lore about the faction's history and bureaucratic nature.

summary.sentence: Adds factions and ships from the game AI War, including the Spire, Neinzul, and Dark Spire, along with new weapons and systems.
summary.paragraph: Introduces three alien factions with unique ships, weapons, and mechanics. The Spire features large crystalline ships with forcefield defenses, while the Neinzul offer organic, EMP-resistant vessels that regenerate hull. A special Vengeance Generator mechanic spawns hostile fleets based on combat activity in specific systems.

summary.sentence: Adds hullmods that allow setting predefined battle commands for AI-piloted ships.
summary.paragraph: Adds hullmods that allow setting predefined battle commands for AI-piloted ships. These commands include retreating based on hull integrity, missile count, peak performance time, or CR level, as well as attacking nearest fighters or retreating when idle. The hullmods cost 0 ordnance points.

summary.paragraph: Adds a new playable faction with several ships, weapons, systems, and missions. The faction specializes in debuffing or disabling enemies and reducing incoming damage, with designs that are mostly midline or high tech. Features include stasis beams and interdiction hullmods to immobilize enemies, compensating for generally poor mobility.

summary.sentence: Adds an advanced autofactory that disassembles and analyzes stored weapons or ships to produce replacements over time.
summary.paragraph: The factory orbits a random planet and replicates goods after analysis, allowing players to secure rare items by trading them in for future production runs. Production times and limits vary based on the size and complexity of the blueprint, with goods sold back at inflated prices. The mod includes extensive configuration options and API support for other modders.

summary.sentence: Adds a variety of new commodities with dynamic pricing and trade fleets across the sector.
summary.paragraph: Introduces new goods that can be traded between systems, each with different prices. Includes extra trade fleets that deliver these goods to random stations, which can be destroyed for loot. Features daily price fluctuations and random permanent price changes for certain goods.

entries.v0.4: The Siegebreaker-class battleship, the Flounder-class artillery destroyer, the Marauder Mk.V revolving cannon, and the Imperator heavy cannon. Also, all ships will now show up in the combat simulator.

summary.sentence: Adds new ships, weapons, and hullmods with unique systems and simulator support.
summary.paragraph: Introduces several new vessels including the Siegebreaker battleship and Flounder destroyer, along with weapons like the Geirskogul shotgun and Marauder cannon. These additions feature modified stats, special abilities such as temporal shells, and integration with the combat simulator.

summary.sentence: Adds Lion's Guard skins to Sindrian Diktat and Lion's Guard ships.
summary.paragraph: This mod provides visual skins for specific ship factions. It has been folded into Ship and Weapon Pack but remains available as an example for first-time modders to study.

summary.sentence: Adds an Odyssey-derived Battlecarrier and Battlecruiser to the game.
summary.paragraph: Introduces two new ship classes: the Ody & Ybo-class Battlecarrier, featuring four wings and two front-arc large energy mounts with a Targeting Feed ship system, and the Yesosey-class Battlecruiser, a broadside vessel with heavy armament that retains the High-Energy Focus system of the Odyssey.

summary.sentence: Adds a new AI faction with unique ships and weapons focused on long-range combat and anti-missile defenses.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Scion Collective, an AI-controlled faction with a diverse fleet including fighters, frigates, destroyers, cruisers, and capital ships. The faction utilizes long-ranged weapons, powerful shields, and burst beam technology. It includes full campaign integration with dynamic battles in specific systems.

Provides different bonuses depending on whether the player is friendly with pirates or not, and includes specific boss ship interactions for compatibility with other mods.

entries.1.4:
Code
- The Valkyrians have finally received their own star system. no longer will they operate from their weird asgard inspired planet in corvus with TO many stations to keep track off.

- Valkyrian Royal Armada has received a makeover, they auto win against all AI fleets, making them immune to death-kiting, they also have unlimited command points, allowing them to have the battlefield advantage regardless of the current situation.
- Their attack level can be modified in their boss file script, in case you think they are annoying or attack too early, their current attack level is 30.

- Made Changes to the Chasing Memories mission.
- Added a few new missions.

- longer cooldown for scorpion MRM and its pod version as well as reduced flight time.
- Slightly nerfed all ballistic point defence.
- Slightly Reduced damage on certain cruise missiles.
- Slightly increased ammo on certain cruise missiles.
- Buffed the Lancer family of weapons.
- Fixed double damage bug on Ether Drive and Ice-Lance cannons.

- All Military variants removed.
- Valkyrian Fleets no longer use Vanilla weapons. balancing them even further.
- Most small Valkyrian point defence for cruisers and capital ships is now built-in, to prevent their exceptional amount of weapon slots from being abused by players, thus much improved faction balance.
- Reduced Ordinance Points for all ships Destroyer class or larger.
- Corrected Supply/day usage of ships.
- Corrected Repair/day usage for ships.

- Decorative blinking lights on Vatican Mk.III, Heron, Almire Mk.II, Almire Mk.III.

- Added NX-K.Max series prototype PD weapon, #made by Maximillianyuen.#
- All high tier fighters have new weapons, greatly balancing them.
- Corrected Supply/day usage of fighters.
- Reduced the size of the ASF fighter.

- All Nirvana class ships now have the Infernium Drive system.
- Burst Drive Replaced with Infernium drive, #made by Cycerin.#
- Incendiary ammunition replaced with Overcharge. increases damage and flux dissipation, but generates hard flux at a very fast rate.
- Added negative effects to the Vessel Modernization hull mod, it was simply an extremely good mod with no drawbacks. increases ship supply and repair per day by 10%.

- Legion Plasma LRM added. #Dark.Revenant modification#
- Removed Herald Destroyer (very old ship that never saw the light of day, a few people may have noticed it in the sprite folder under the name of "Limbo".)
- Almire Mk.III added. (last "combat" ship in the mod, no more will be added, i have too many ships as it is.)
- 2 rear small PD on Yoshura II removed, slightly new engine and hull design, all small PD is built in.
- Almire Mk.II changes: -2 large mounts, +2 medium mounts.
- Sequence added.
- Heron remodeled.
entries.1.3C:
- Removed a whole bunch of sound files that has been either replaced or simply not been used, should shrink the size of the mod considerably.

- Added shader support for Valkyrians, the mod now requires Shaderlib. (will be listen in the OP)
- Valkyrians now have their own engine sounds. (although they dont work properly because SS dosn't fully support this yet.)

- Added relations to all the wonderful new mods and factions out there, Valkyrians, once again, hate everybody.
- Updated Convoy shopping list.
- Updated Boss fleet reward list.

- New Mission: King's bane, very similar to sinking the bis'mar, but considerably harder.
- New mission: Battle for Heaven's Gate, fairly difficult mission that requires you to keep a close watch on the tactical screen and avoid losing ships to win.

- Added lore for Yoshura Mk.II ships that have served with the faction. found at the bottom of the ships codex.

- Prototype variant of Nirvana MK.II part of royal armada.
- Remade some variants to include the ether driver.

- Altered micro burn drive a little bit, there is a slight drift after the burn is over that graduably goes back to the ships own top speed from 50% of the burn speed, alowing you to move around the battlefield much faster.

- changed gun facing on radiance's 2 large side turrets, all 3 could shot straight forward.
- Remodeled Lightning Assault Fighter.
- Added Firefly Laser Fighter.
- Remodeled Ancord into a heavy bomber, old ship removed.
- Further improved Infinity ASF Fighter. (its big...very big)

- Several new sounds on standby.
- New sounds for Laser Blasters.
- New sound for Cruise missile's launch stage.
- New Sprite for Antiproton Laser Battery.

- Slightly reduced projectile speed and rate of fire on all weapons.
- Increased OP on Wraith missile from 5 to 6 to balance it, it was simply a much stronger harpoon for the same cost.
- New weapon PTR-GT Laser, for Certain Frigates and fighters.
- New Missile: Sunfury Torpedo.
- New Missile: Shadow LRCM.
- New weapon: Ice-Lance (dosn't work the way its supposed to.)
- Reduced damage on AP Mega beam cannon by 200.

- Changed large mount on Nirvana Mk.III to a medium mount.
entries.1.3B:
- Prefixes are done. compatebility for everybody! (and holy *** did it take a long time, remind me never to do that again.)

- Decorative blinking lights on Nirvana Mk.II. (Yay Cycerin)

- frigates costs the same as before to deploy.
- Super-capitals costs the same as before to deploy, "such decisive weapons should not be squandered."
- repairs are doubbled in accordance to the 6.2 update, and CR to deploy has been lowered on "most" ships,

- Vatican Mk.III has recieved a facelift (cheers MShadowy) 2 hangars added. it now shares the equal highest flight deck count with the Astral and the Hildolfr(Neutrino).

- added a description to what the Command-Relay system does, as it was rather shady before.

- Added another built in hull mod, Electronic Superiority, makes Super-Capital ships immune to EMP damage. (for now, supposed to stop scripted E-War, like my ECM Jammer)

- Increased the cost of Yoshura Mk.II to half a million credits.
- Increased max Hull by 1000. "27500 -> 28500"
- Increased Top Speed for Yoshura Mk.II from 20 to 25SU/s
- Yoshura Mk.II AI will activate its shipsystem at 60% remaining hull instead of 50%, to give it a bigger chance of surviving.
- Yoshura Mk.II has recieved a facelift (cheers MShadowy) Badassness on a whole new level.

- Radiance has recieved a facelift (cheers MShadowy) +2 medium mounts and moved large mounts forward. 2 medium and 2 small missiles removed, replaced with 2 large foward facing cannons.

- Implemented beam particle effects. (Yay Cycerin)
  
- +2 small ballistics to Elysium, both foward facing.

- the light A.P beam cannon is now a medium weapon (was intended to be so from the start)

- new suppression weapon, Twin HI-IR Laser, long range and a steady fire rate.
- New drone model for Valkyrian combat drones.
- Renamed "Desperate Defence" to "Valiant Defence"

 (both of these are very much WIP, and are on hold, dont expect them to show up any time soon)
- New model for Infinity in the making. (currently only in the simulator and in one of the missions, VERY overpowered)
- New heavy bomber in the making.

- Further increased supply cost of all ships.

- Increased the cost of Azmodaeus to 7.5 million credits. (supposed to be unattainable)

- I think i wrote some stuff in the previous versions list by mistake, so if something is new there, it should have been here. =)

summary.sentence: Adds a new independent military faction with unique ships, weapons, and lore.
summary.paragraph: Adds the Valkyrians, a fanatical military superpower focused on superiority and control. The mod introduces numerous new ships ranging from frigates to super-capitals, along with custom weapons, hull mods, and missions. It includes detailed lore, faction strengths and weaknesses, and compatibility with other mods like Exerelin, LazyLib, and ShaderLib.

summary.sentence: Combines multiple faction mods into a single, easy-to-install package with vanilla-style balance.
summary.paragraph: Provides a pre-configured collection of inter-compatible faction mods, saving users the effort of checking compatibility between individual additions. The compilation includes factions such as the Kadur Theocracy, Bushi, and Neutrino Corporation, all balanced to feel fairly vanilla. It is also compatible with Exerelin for those who wish to use that framework alongside the included mods.

entries.1.3: Optimizations EVERYWHERE. Now requires ShaderLib as well as LazyLib. Updated all mods. Removed Kadur. Removed Interstellar Federation. Made all fleets in the sector generally bigger. Made a lot of changes so that fleets are spawned around the player location, making huge number of fleets per system possible. Added more types of fleets. Added Construction Rigs to big fleets. Made mining fleet actually stick to an asteroid. Made blueprints a bit rarer and crew slaves a bit more common. Completely reworked the Station interface for infinitely better usability. Fixed limited storage BUG for the SECRET station. Added a bounty hunt system for all factions (plus independents). Added confirmation dialogues for joining and leaving factions. BPs are now displayed by ship type, not faction. New modification system that allows you to change a ship into a similar one (tarsus-condor for example). You can also set any ship of your fleet to be aggressive/passive by default. Everytime your relationship changes (joining or leaving a faction for example) you get a complete report on the current statuses. Implemented a randomized variant maker so that any ship can be equipped in every possible way(inside the faction's weapons and ships lists). Fixed a BUG that didn't properly assign a flagship to AI fleets. Made loot drops a bit rarer. Made the start a bit harder. Added cool battle graphic effects thanks to Dark Revenant (anamorphic flares, explosions).
entries.1.2: Added Mayorate, Interstellar Federation, Infernal Machine. Loads of fixes and quality of life upgrades (eg. production queue) . New start. Updated stats and compatibility for 0.6.2a (all ships have updated stats, until modders fix them officially). All mods up to date (JP, TuP, etc).
entries.1.1c: Fixed missing Pirate Plus ships' values for campaign integration. Scaled up the cost in resources for bigger ships (now they cost roughly as vanilla).

summary.sentence: Combines a curated selection of mods into a single, balanced campaign with enhanced difficulty and lore integration.
summary.paragraph: Integrates various factions and mods into a vanilla sector, featuring solid bounty systems, dynamic stations, and a complex craft system with blueprints. It includes a reworked loot and spawn system with infinite variants, fleet leveling, and new graphic effects. The mod aims to enhance the vanilla experience with greater difficulty and achievement feel while maintaining balance.

summary.sentence: Adds debris clouds containing excess loot from defeated fleets for scavenging.
summary.paragraph: Adds a trading and economy focused feature where fleets drop debris clouds with leftover loot after battles. This allows players to scavenge remnants from AI fleets, with the debris dissipating after approximately three stellar days. It also aims to make non-combat professions like scavenging more interesting.

entries.Build 34:
Fixes:
1.  Big bug with Boarding Teleporters.
2.  Big (very old) bug with Hardened Electronics; it actually does what it says on the tin now.

Changes:
1.  Armor Regeneration eventually "wears out" after taking a lot of damage, instead of being permanent invulnerability under some circumstances.
entries.Build 33:
Adds:
1. Upgraded to ShaderLib 1.52a, which should resolve some slowdown issues for a few folks.
2. Accelerated Ammo Feed has an AI that is specific to it.

Fixes:

1.  Several missing / incorrect descriptions.
2.  Brawler AI works correctly on Frigates.
3.  Thor and Odin actually work correctly now.  Warning: this makes the Gaians pretty hard to beat with shield-tanks.
4.  Boarding Teleporters will no longer magically give you two captures sometimes, and the captured ships are automatically marked as Mothballed to prevent CR disruption.
5.  Wages work correctly again.
6.  Various other little stuff I can't be bothered to document.

Changes:
1.  Repair Gantries now stacks.
2.  Rebal on Slugger, Slugthrower; Slugger is now better than Thumper, but costs more OPs, Slugthrower is slightly more useful for OP cost vs. Thumper, but I'll probably re-visit the OP cost on it again later.
entries.Build 32:
New Features:
1.  Forget where your Bounties are?  Get a list of current Bounty Missions at all times from Stations.
2.  Tired of having to use that Germanium slider?  Just hit "get all".
3.  Don't want to fight that weak fleet you just encountered?  Hit Leave.

Improvements:
1.  Stations will no longer get destroyed / change owners until players have reached level 3, to make things more stable for newbies.
2.  The initial "payday" has been delayed a little more at the start of play.
3.  Heavy Armor, Neutronium Plating and Core Removal give a small buff to base Armor values, not just a multiplier.

Fixes:
1.  Escape scenario actually works right, finally, for both sides.
2.  Fixes for a bunch of missing / unhelpful descriptions.
3.  Fix for the Sniper and Brawler AIs' collision-avoidance sub-AIs.
4.  Various other fixes for AIs related to retreating.
5.  Fixed some smallish issues relating to damage code in certain edge-case scenarios.  In general, AOE-type and Plasma-type weapons should work quite reliably now.

entries.1.21:
- Updated hullParser from Omnifactory 1.5.
- Fixed the wrong constructor being selected when adding a new ship to the recycling or production collection.
entries.1.2:
- fixed bug in Complex Parts Compiler resoulting in 217 entries missing.
- GenAdvInfo has been updated with these entries and fleet control v 1.15 (requires you to start a new game).
- You can specify in AddOmniFac.java what resources the complex can convert and how efficiently. This supports any resource, including those from other mods.
- By default, Fuel (18 C/M), Supplies (12 C/M), Ore (12 C/M, from Fleet Control mod) and Unconverted Materials (1.2 C/M, from Freighter Start mod) are added.
- Spawn logic has been "simplified" to spawn you in the asteroidbelt in Corvus or the equal distance from the sun in a different system. Better make sure to prepare a warm welcome or get your engines tuned for when you pass by the pirate bases.
- A mini-mod named "Freighter Start" can be optionally downloaded. It allows you to start with a Buffalo freighter and a large amount of Unconverted Materials if used with this mod. It is not useful in combat for anything than retreating (and is even bad at that). It does however enable you to transport a lot of resources at once, which is useful once you start getting a production running.
- Material value is now constant untill it reaches the ceiling. This way, it should be more intuitive to judge the efficiency of an item. If a weapon has a basevalue that is 40 % of the ceiling then its B/M will also be 40 % of the max possible B/M.
- B/M at the ceiling has been changed 50 instead of 75. This is to decrease the change of getting a decimal material value resoulting in an inacurate B/M when an item was above the ceiling.
- Construction time has been changed to start at a minimum day depending on size and increase linearly to twice as much untill it reaches a ceiling based of its base value. From there it will progress deminishing potentionally.
- The ceiling for ship material value has been changed to 4000 / 13600 / 34680 / 78608 / 167042. The ceiling for ship construction time is 3333 / 9714 / 21675 / 43671 / 83521.
- The ceiling for weapon construction time is the same as for material value which is unchagned.
entries.1.1:
- Fixed null error when you stored a ship in the Omni Shipyard which didn't exist in the Omni Factory.
- Fuel and supplies can be converted to material at a rate of 60 purchase value / material (C/M), 10 supplies equals 1 material and 5 fuel equals 2 material.
- Material and construction use seperate calculations.
- Construction time of ships heavily reduced, unless they are expensive and/or have a high requirement.
- Base value / material (B/M) of an item will increase with an items base value untill it reaches 70 B/M. These are the base values at which an item reaches 70 B/M: 600 / 2040 / 11800 for weapons and 3000 / 11100 / 30800 / 75950 / 175700 for ships.
- When an item is added to the Omni Recycle Facility, a message will be shown with the items C/M.
- The message shown when an item is added to the Omni Factory also contains the sell value / material (I/M) of the item.
- If a new item is added to the Omni Recycle Facility or Omni Factory, then a message with the average profit / material will be shown.
- The Omni Recycle Facility will have a "supply" like Available Materials called Average Value per Material showing the average C/M of the station (does not include already converted material).
- The Omni Factory also have an Average Value per Material showing the average I/M of the station.
Note: To maximize the profit of the complex, you would want the C/M to be as low as possible (assuming you didn't "get" it for free) while I/M should be as high as possible (63 is max). If you're only worried about upgrading stuff, then you should multiply C/M with 0.75.

The package also includes instructions for fixing blurry text on Retina displays by modifying the launch script.

entries.1.3:
Some ship tweaks, fixes, and new ships!
 Ships Added
Capitals:
Grant
Cruisers:
Ogopogo

 Tweaks and fixes:

Mokele-Mbembe armor reduced from 1650 to 1250, advanced targeting core removed, and health reduced from 36000 to 30000. Flux Capacity reduced from 25000 to 20000 and flux distribution reduced from 1000 to 800. I'll be honest, I really over-tuned this thing. I was successfully taking on multiple paragons while running what is essentially a civilian mining hulk. It should still be tough, but not "I Win Every Fight by Myself" Tough. I have also changed two of its hybrid large mounts to ballistic large mounts in an attempt to prevent myself from slapping on 4 tachyon lances and calling it as well as opening the door for a more hybrid playstyle and more chances for its small and medium mounts to shine.

DP and supplies cost drop for a few civilian-grade ships. Mokele-Mbembe down to 50 from 60. Behemoth and Leviathan both to 16 from 18. Koolakamba down to 3.

Leviathan, Buford, and Meade now have proper hints for AI in their ship data file. Should be much less "rush in and die" from the escort carriers.

Mooncracker Laser should no longer show up in random loot as it should now no longer be able to drop.

Sliderock and Koolakamba ships should now properly show up in civilian fleets and Independent markets.

Koolakamba and Sliderocks' shields will now no longer instantly flux out the ship because it costs 50 to 100 times its flux dissipation to run. Whoopsie.

Slugworth ships should now show up less in direct combat fleets. Seriously they were everywhere.

All unaligned and industrial styled ships in this mod pack now have blue or yellow weapons covers respectively to prevent the eye-sore that was low-tech weapons covers on ships that aren't low tech colors.

Grammar pass. Seriously, some of the descriptions were pretty bad. This pass hopefully fixed some of it.

summary.sentence: Adds numerous new ships and weapons for the unaligned powers of the Persean Sector.

Ships feature unique roles ranging from civilian mining hulks to escort carriers and pirate vessels.

The UNSC focuses on missiles and ballistics with unique MAC weapons, while the Covenant features high-tech, high-flux ships. Players can choose from five unique factions plus pirates, each with distinct ship classes, weapon preferences, and tactical roles.

entries.0.9.2:
Code
 This is my first mod I did to test LLMs and give me an intro into the modding in this game, took me way more time than expected,
the game didn't first supported what I wanted to do initially and I had to adapt, some feature creep and some AI hallucinations eventually
resulted on this.
I’m pretty picky with mods. I usually stick to the developer’s original vision, since mods can easily mess with the overall feel of the game.
Anything that breaks immersion is a dealbreaker for me. That said, I’m really happy with this one. It fits naturally into my vanilla
experience and improves it without getting in the way.
The exporter rebate is a workaround, but a necessary one. It might seem odd at first, but compared to how extreme the vanilla
export tariffs are, it actually feels like justice xD

If you have feedback or tips on improving modding in starsector it will be much appreciated, and will consider changes that make sense.
I’ve also got a few more mod ideas in mind to improve some bad gameplay designs, hope you find this mod useful!

Makes enemy ships use these liveries so that variants of ships look different. Enhances ship sprites to add lighting or polish.

mods.name: Thorough System Scan(was System Wide Sensor Scan)

extras.saveCompatibility: Can be added mid safe.

summary.sentence: Adds a campaign ability to scan an entire star system for salvageable objects and fleet positions at the cost of volatiles and time.
summary.paragraph: Adds an initially available campaign ability that allows the player to perform a System-Scale Sensor Burst after meeting prerequisites such as fleet sensor strength and volatile cargo. The scan reveals salvageable objects and temporarily tracks all fleets in the system, while making the player fleet highly visible and reducing the readiness of sensor-providing ships.

summary.sentence: Provides file edits to Starsector that remove balance mechanics.
summary.paragraph: This mod consists of file edits for Starsector. It removes balance from the game, embracing a chaotic playstyle described as praising the holy barcode.

summary.sentence: Provides an IRC library that accesses Twitch viewer information for other mods.
summary.paragraph: This library anonymously logs into Twitch IRC to track viewers joining and leaving a channel. It serves as a foundation for other mods to integrate Twitch data, such as viewer counts, into the game.

summary.sentence: Changes crew composition at markets based on Twitch viewership.
summary.paragraph: When docking at a market, crew members join or leave based on changes in the number of Twitch viewers. The baseline is set the first time you dock after starting or loading a game.

entries.v1.2:
- Fixed LunaLib detection to use isModEnabled() - more reliable than the previous approach (thanks WolframSegler!)
- Added Version Checker support
- Renamed setting to "Supply Reduction Percent" for clarity
entries.v1.1: - Added optional LunaLib support for configurable supply reduction percentage

summary.sentence: Eliminates supply consumption for ships while orbiting planets, stations, or other bodies.
summary.paragraph: Ships consume zero supplies for maintenance while in orbit. Normal supply consumption resumes automatically upon leaving orbit. The mod works passively without requiring user input and supports optional configuration via LunaLib.

mods.name: Reverse Collapse: Codename Bakery Portraits Pack

extras.saveCompatibility: Should be safe to download and drop right into your modpack.

summary.sentence: Adds portraits of characters from Reverse Collapse: Codename Bakery for the player faction along with faction flags.
summary.paragraph: Includes a light portraits pack featuring characters from the game, primarily for the player faction. Also adds eight flags from factions encountered throughout the story. The pack contains less than 100 items and is safe to add to an existing modpack.

extras.saveCompatibility: Yes.

summary.sentence: Changes the Commerce industry to be a structure that saves an industry slot and provides configurable income bonuses and stability penalties.
summary.paragraph: Replaces the Commerce industry with a structure to free up an industry slot, allowing a market on every colony without sacrificing industry capacity. It adjusts commerce bonuses and penalties to be more reasonable and realistic. Users can customize the income bonuses and stability penalties through Lunalib settings.

extras.saveCompatibility: Safe to add to a save, not safe to remove.

summary.sentence: Adds multiple carrier core hullmods and configurable features to enhance fighter management and combat capabilities.
summary.paragraph: Introduces various hullmods that modify carrier performance, such as increased fighter bays, buffed wings, and improved mobility or range. Includes configurable options for fighter auto-return, formation attacks, and speed adjustments. Requires LunaLib to function.

summary.sentence: Provides a version of the carrier mod that removes most hullmods while keeping specific configurable features.
summary.paragraph: Retains the Steady Bombing Protocol and Conservative Deployment hullmods but removes the others. Keeps the configurable non-hullmod features like fighter auto-return and formation settings. Designed for players who find the full hullmod set too disruptive or overpowered.

summary.sentence: Allows viewing logs from starsector.log inside the game via a scroller text renderer or the Console Commands mod.
summary.paragraph: Displays logs on the top left of the screen with sound effects when they appear. It also allows viewing logs in the console of the Console Commands mod. The mod is configurable and intended to assist mod developers by showing error logs exactly when they happen.

entries.0.1.2:
1. Added the Ithica Research Institute, and planned to completely reset all ship maps and various things [but the balance was not done]
2. The look and feel of Krausm’s weapons has been greatly optimized
3. Omega partial ship map and engine fine-tuning
4. The Omega fleet refresh in the Omega galaxy has become normal, and there will no longer be a situation where there are five pages of Omegas [there are five now, so you can use a normal fleet to challenge them].
5. Temporarily removed Omega invasion and other codes to prevent possible errors [will not be moved back until I think it is fixed]
6. Some balance adjustments are better than nothing
7. New Pie
entries.0.1.0:
1. Added a large number of ship skills and Magic bounty
2. Fixed several bugs that may cause crashes
3. Texture and collision box repair, while trying to enhance AI performance
entries.0.0.9:
The refreshable ships of the Krausm Concept Design Bureau have been balanced, and the script plot will be added gradually.
Currently you can find a nebula to the west of the core star field, and that is where they are located.
(In fact, you will also see a white gravitational field there, which is the actual entrance. Because the current galaxy hegemony will forcibly send troops to the faction, resulting in Null, we have no choice but to reopen various jump points. We will try to fix this in the future. In the end, players can only rely on the horizontal axis to enter this galaxy)
But if you wander far enough, you will find another white gravity field in the space not far from the Krausm system - probably in the hyperspace storm group - before going down, I suggest you save once. Because you may encounter some unexpected enemies in this mod.
1. Further adjust the battle balance
(Jackol) 2. I really don't know how to make a driver's license, so the moon phase is temporarily exposed in the opening super battleship of Krausm.
3. To prevent the end from being blown up, additional colonies were placed for Krausm

summary.sentence: Adds two new playable factions, new super vessels, and hidden galaxy content to the game.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Krausm Concept Design Bureau and Omega Trauma factions with new ships and systems. Includes hidden galaxy exploration and encounters with powerful Omega vessels. Adds new ship skills, balance adjustments, and various bug fixes.

summary.sentence: Adds two new ships and a mission to the Lion's Guard fleet.
summary.paragraph: Adds the Conquest Mk II (LG) with a built-in Thermal Pulse Cannon and the Champion (LG) with an energy front hardpoint. Includes a mission to test the Conquest Mk II against an Independent mercenary. Features custom flashy effects and art by King Alfonzo.

- Compiled for Java 17 and Kotlin 2.0

- Fixes a save corrupting issue (present in Kaysaar's Toolbox Edition)

summary.sentence: Adds RPG-style upgrades and exotic components to ships and enemies that do not consume hullmod slots.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to install upgrades on ships and enemies to make them harder, better, faster, and stronger. These upgrades require common materials like metal and transplutonics, as well as special items found through research and mining stations. Each ship has a limit to the number of upgrades it can install.

entries.1.7.2: -Increased the Cataphact, the Hawk and the Wolf EX shield boundary.

summary.sentence: Adds new ships, variants, weapons, fighters, and bombers to the game.
summary.paragraph: Adds 2 new ships, 6 variant ships from Vanilla, 1 Fighter, 1 Bomber, 1 interceptor and 9 weapons. Independents know the ship's blueprints, and the weapons and fighters are rare blueprints in the wild. This mod's ships and weapons are designed to be superior to vanilla.

summary.sentence: Adds an end-game expansion focused on recovering and utilizing advanced sector technology through disassembling and assembling Omega weapons.
summary.paragraph: Allows players to disassemble Omega weapons to obtain components, which can then be used to assemble other Omega weapons or salvage Omega ships. The mod supports all vanilla Omega weapons and mod-added weapons using the Omega tag, with future plans to include Nexerelin starts and additional Remnant content options.

summary.sentence: Adds Tauri, Lantean, and Goauld ships with custom weapons and market availability to Starsector.
summary.paragraph: Introduces nine Tauri ships, four Lantean ships, and one Goauld ship, each equipped with custom weapons like Lantean drones and Asgard beams. Most ships can spawn in markets, though Lantean vessels are recommended to appear as derelicts due to their power. The Tauri faction is functional with available blueprints, though they lack a dedicated spawn point.

summary.sentence: Allows players to destroy, decimate, turn to pirates, or make independent the vanilla factions at new game start.
summary.paragraph: This mod provides options to alter the status of vanilla factions such as the Hegemony, Tritachyon, and others when starting a new game. Effects include destroying their planets and stations, weakening them, converting their colonies to pirates, or making them independent. It also includes a secondary function to cap colony sizes at 8 or a user-defined maximum.

summary.sentence: Adds a hullmod that allows ships to dock with carriers for repair and replenishment when damaged or out of ammo.
summary.paragraph: Adds a hullmod that allows you to be able to dock with any carrier larger than a frigate. Once you lose 20% of your hull HP, fall below 40% CR, or run out of ammunition, you can turn on autopilot and your ship will navigate to its assigned carrier and land to repair and replenish.

summary.sentence: Provides Spanish, Turkish, and French translations for the Starsector 0.98a-RC8 base game and several popular mods.
summary.paragraph: This project translates the core game and various mods into Spanish, Turkish, and French. It includes specific files for the base game and combined files for mods. The Turkish translation notes a game engine limitation regarding character rendering.

summary.sentence: Adds a configurable UI overlay to the campaign map that displays faction relationship status and changes.
summary.paragraph: Displays faction lists and relationship status directly on the navigation screen, sorted logically by alignment. Allows users to toggle the list, adjust its size and text scaling, and apply filters for hostile factions or current-system presence. Provides visual feedback for relationship deltas and offers automation options for showing and hiding the overlay.

summary.sentence: Fixes rendering slowdown issues with the Heron's Targeting Feed system by removing the shield glow effect while maintaining weapons glow on shielded fighters.
summary.paragraph: This small quality of life mod addresses a rendering slowdown some graphics cards experience with the Targeting Feed system. It removes the shield glow effect to improve performance but keeps the weapons glow on shielded fighters to preserve visual identification when the system is active.

entries.1.2.0:
Adds 1 hullmod, and 1 fighter wing.

Hullmod can be found during exploration, and wing is sold in independant/pirate/black market.

Apply hullmod to a ship, and the wing will become that ship!

LPC OP cost will dynamically change. Currently it is (DP Cost)*5. Example : https://imgur.com/a/ag8eZFO

summary.sentence: Adds a hullmod and fighter wing that lets players create custom LPCs in-game.
summary.paragraph: Adds a hullmod and fighter wing that lets players create custom LPCs in-game. The hullmod can be found during exploration, and the wing is sold in independent, pirate, or black market locations. Applying the hullmod to a ship makes the wing become that ship, with LPC OP cost dynamically changing based on DP cost.

summary.paragraph: Adds a custom start with a version of the Djoeng Voidfaring Hubship from Indies Expansion, recreated from scratch without requiring the expansion itself. The ship can be upgraded with permanent improvements, swappable weapon or fighter bay modules, and ultimate system options. Includes a new sprite vision and the ability to restart the upgrade journey if the ship is lost.

summary.sentence: Adds a separate Guardian ship variant with a built bridge, a blueprint, and the Automated ship hull mod removed for player use.
summary.paragraph: This mod introduces a unique Guardian ship that features a bridge structure and lacks the automated hull modification, allowing the player to pilot it directly. The ship costs 80dp to field and 1.5 million credits to build, reflecting its retained autoforge and enhanced strength. The release includes three new variants: Full Energy, Full Ballistic, and Full Missile, each with distinct point costs and build prices.

summary.sentence: Adds a collection of hullmods that augment, revert, rectify, or upgrade existing ship capabilities.
summary.paragraph: Adds numerous hullmods organized into categories such as Augmentations for boosting flux and OP, Reversions to undo negative effects of built-in hullmods, and Rectifications to mitigate penalties. Includes upgrade suites for flux coils and radiators, stopgaps to counter D-Mods, and diagnostic tools for fleet management. Some features have a soft dependency on Starship Legends for reputation-based installation requirements.

entries.v0.4.0:
Ships:

-Changes:
--Cteno:
---Replaced two small ballistics mounts with energy ones because it kept bothering me that the ship had to use two different types of small PD.
---Replaced the Entropy Amplifier system with Twinned Interdictor Arrays.
(It's the same as the unused vanilla one, except you get two charges at the cost of slightly slower recharge.)

--Urocerus:
---Touched-up the sprite so the spinal cannon actually looks spinal instead of just being a turret on a hardpoint.
---Swapped a small ballistics slot for an energy slot.
---Replaced the Plasma Burn system with a variant that looks slightly different but is mechanically the same.

--Chalice:
---Touched-up the sprite so the spinal cannon actually looks spinal instead of just being a turret on a hardpoint.

Weapons:

-Added:
--Added the Paratrech and Parapon fighters.
--Preno PD Autopulser
--Eciton Laser Emitter
--Masari Pulse Cannon
--Several non-factional "Blueprint-Hacked" weapons for occasional use by independents and mercenaries.

-Changes:
--Various minor adjustments I forgot to note down, sorry.

--Nitor Particle Lance:
---Range reduced to 1000 (was 1200).

--Vivax Plasma Launcher
---Renamed to Cresson Plasma Launcher
(builtin weapons generally follow a theme of being named after the specific name of an insect species in the genus the ship it belongs to is named after. for example, the Xyloc is named after the genus Xylocopa, while its builtin weapon the Combusta is named after the species Xylocopa combusta. The Vivax was originally meant to be a standalone weapon before I decided to make it a builtin of the Urocerus, but haven't bothered to change the name until now.)
--Increased flux cost to 5000 (was 3500). It was a bit too efficient for its range and damage, especially given its lore.

--Brachypter fighter
---Sprite-update.
---Changed formation to diamond (was claw).

Other:
-Added a unique ship name pool for AA, as well as some new names for Pirate and Pather ships as former AA citizens who turned to piracy or terrorism kept using the naming scheme.
-Adjusted the market modifiers on Apocrita. The jungle planet is actually habitable now, and has slightly better farmlands.
-Adjusted doctrine to never try using phase ships, use more carriers and field more, lower quality ships. Make them a bit more swarmy to fit the theme better.
-Made certain things Codex Unlockable.
-Added Commissioned Crews support.
-Made the Calcari and Alyro systems no longer spawn if you're using Nexerelin's random core worlds option. This should fix other factions potentially starting with colonies Apocrita, Ymenn and Oruss despite AA already having colonies on them (thanks to Timid and Vexlia Artemiss for helping me sort this out).
-Added a big list of what everything  was named after in the files, for anyone who cares about etymology or bugs. spoilers, it's mostly bugs. why yes, i AM neurodivergent.
entries.v0.3.2:
Weapons:

-Combusta Stinger:
--Damage per second reduced to 1800 (was 2000).
(It was basically a Tachyon Lance with less range and no EMP but more raw damage. As a normal weapon that may have been fine but the Xyloc is agile enough that it is not quite enough. It still has more raw damage than a TL but its less efficient now. It's meant to be a mining tool, so I think that makes it match the Mining Blaster more too?)

-Aculeus SRM Tube:
--Reduced flight time to 1.3 seconds (was 20s).
(This was an error that resulted in the range being less limited than intended)

-Aurifer Pulse Cannon
--Damage reduced to 500 (was 600).
--Energy per shot increased to 600 (was 500).
--Chargedown increased to 1s (was 0.8s).
(The Aurifer was a powerful and efficient main weapon on its own, and became downright broken with Flux Recycling. The decreased efficiency and fire rate should make it less powerful but still serviceable normally while not being quite as broken while Flux Recycling is active.)

Ships:
-Several frigates now cost +1 DP. I forgot to write down which ones, sorry.

-Sceliphron:
--Flux dissipation reduced to 400 (was 500).

-Mutill:
--Flux dissipation reduced to 500 (was 600).

-Polistes:
--Flux Recycling system cooldown increased to 10s (was 8s).

Other:
-Adjusted a bounty's reward scaling and base value.
entries.v0.3.1:

--Increased flux per shot to 300 (was 250).

-Tristis Pulse Gun:
--Increased flux per shot to 120 (was 100).

--Added 'restricted' tag so it should no longer appear randomly, only as a bounty reward.
--Increased flux per shot to 1000 (was 900).

Ships:

-Slightly debuffed the shield efficiency of some non-pilotable bounty ships.
-Adjusted shield module placement and module shield arc on a non-pilotable bounty ship.

summary.sentence: Adds a small faction with 14 ships, 15 non-built-in weapons, 3 fighters, and 7 High-Value Bounties.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Apocrita Association, a faction featuring ships focused on built-in weapons. The mod includes various ship classes like frigates, destroyers, cruisers, and capitals, along with pirate and Persean League variants. It also adds new weapons, fighters, and a bounty system that can be discovered at markets or through specific game conditions.

summary.sentence: Adds Lion Guard ship variants and weapons to the Sindrian Diktat faction.
summary.paragraph: This mod makes Lion Guard variants easier to obtain by adding them to the Sindrian Diktat. It also makes the associated weapons sellable. A separate addon is available to include variants from Dark Revenant's Ship/Weapon Pack.

mods.name: Lion Guard for all (Ship/Weapon Pack addition)

summary.sentence: Adds Lion Guard variants from Dark Revenant's Ship/Weapon Pack to the Sindrian Diktat.
summary.paragraph: This addon extends the main mod to include additional variants from a separate pack. It requires the base Lion Guard for all mod to function correctly.

extras.saveCompatibility: REQUIRES NEW SAVE

summary.sentence: Adds a Stargate-inspired human faction with new ships, weapons, hullmods, a trinary star system, and unique ZPM-based industry mechanics.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the United Nations Space Force faction, featuring ships, weapons, and hullmods inspired by Stargate lore. Includes a new trinary star system, Stargate industry mechanics with ZPM upgrades, and extensive background lore detailing the faction's origins and survival.

entries.1.0.1:
Fix to native RC bug where cosmetic (0 damage) weapons cause ships to gain infinite flux and invisible, invincible shields. I've confirmed that ASF's Cockatrice no longer causes it.
As a side effect, all beams deal a minimum of 0.01 damage which hopefully doesn't change much.
Shield 'breakthrough' effect limited to >0.01 to assist in preventing infinite shields bug.
Beam weapon's minimum damage post-threshold increased from 1 to 2, due to beam damage being halved when calculating penetration.
Default settings for missile ammo reset to vanilla values. Still can be changed in settings.

summary.sentence: Rewrites combat mechanics to behave more like vanilla Starsector with increased weapon ranges, adjusted damage formulas, and configurable settings.
summary.paragraph: Increases weapon ranges and decreases spread while making ships slightly faster but with worse handling. Adjusts armor angling, damage thresholds, and beam weapon damage falloff to emulate a more realistic yet playable combat experience. Includes detailed configuration options for projectile, beam, and missile weapons.

summary.sentence: Adds a small, insular faction with unique ships, weapons, and missions that revolve around AI integration and repatriating AI cores.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Epsilon Pact, a faction located north-west of the core systems that includes AI cores in their definition of living beings. The mod adds ten unique ships with powerful burst damage and fragile defenses, twelve modular weapons with scripted behaviors, and seven menu missions to establish lore. Players can exchange AI cores for Pact blueprints and encounter new contacts and fleet compositions.

summary.sentence: Reduces the size of Sabot and Harpoon weapon racks.
summary.paragraph: This mini-mod adjusts the visual scale of Sabot and Harpoon racks to make them less prominent. It is designed to improve the aesthetic balance of these weapon systems.

summary.sentence: Adds 30+ achievements and 20+ cosmetic paintjobs to MagicLib's framework.
summary.paragraph: This mod provides a collection of achievements that track player progress within a game install, similar to Steam achievements. It also includes over 20 unlockable paintjobs for fleet customization. The achievements are designed to offer a sense of accomplishment without granting gameplay advantages, while the paintjobs are purely cosmetic sprite swaps.

summary.sentence: Adds new unique items to scavenge from abandoned space stations, planet ruins, salvage fields, and derelict ships.
summary.paragraph: Introduces specific loot that replaces generic categories like ore or luxury items to make scavenging more rewarding. The alternative version expands these drops to include salvage fields and post-battle salvage, though it may also cause items to appear in nonhuman fleets.

entries.v0.6.1: Implemented fleet greetings and flavor text for relation levels in the faction intel screen, added description to the Champion (A) (TLL). Fixed Codex description for the AI Switch hullmod. Changed faction fleet prefix from TLL to TDF. Added custom rank names.

summary.sentence: Adds a new faction with unique ships, hullmods, and AI switching capabilities.
summary.paragraph: Introduces the Tellasian League faction, featuring custom ships and the AI Switch hullmod that allows ships to be crewed by human or AI captains. Includes Nexerilin and Commissioned Crews functionality, along with custom fleet greetings and relation text.

Introduces the Knights Arbiter boss faction that spawns in random systems and drops blueprints for their Remnant-based ships and weapons. summary.sentence: Adds a hullmod that prevents specific ships from being restored by the Hull Restoration skill.
summary.paragraph: This mod introduces a hullmod that makes ships unrestorable, meaning D-mods will not be removed over time by Hull Restoration. It allows players to keep D-mods on certain ships for benefits like Derelict Operations or lower DP, while still using Hull Restoration on other vessels.

summary.paragraph: Introduces several massive vessels that are not easily acceptable in the vanilla game, making the experience more difficult for players. These ships are intended for vanilla factions and include various juggernauts and battlecarriers with unique stats and roles.

summary.sentence: Adds automatic saving on jump, transaction, and after battle, with configurable normal saves.
summary.paragraph: Provides an updated autosave system that creates saves during specific game events such as jumping, trading, and combat. It utilizes new autosave slots and allows users to configure when normal saves occur through Luna settings. By default, all autosaves are enabled while normal saves remain disabled.

summary.sentence: Adds a building that automates the reclamation of wrecks and debris fields within a colony's star system.
summary.paragraph: The Salvage Office scans for derelicts and post-battle remains every three days to collect fuel, supplies, and D-hulls. It can also recover ships and salvage various materials like AI cores, blueprints, weapons, and drones. The system ignores mission-critical objects and non-playable ships.

The names are categorized and weighted by faction to match their thematic feel, covering first names, last names, and dual-use options. The mod is purely additive and compatible with other mods and mod managers.

Requires the Neutrino Detector to pinpoint specific objects. Objects that are detectable include derelict ships, weapons/supply caches, and mining/research stations.

summary.paragraph: Adds several very OP ships ranging from medium to massive sizes and one powerful cannon. The ships are bashed together using public resources.

entries.1.0.2:
Soundfix: Omega-state soundscape tuned — no longer annoying.
Defensive fighter boons: Player fighters now have increased HP and deal more damage to missiles and fighters from the start. These values are configurable in balancedata.yaml.
entries.1.0.1:
Combat Momentum Reworked: Completely streamlined into 6 distinct levels plus 1 ultimate state. Cleaner escalation, sharper feedback, faster pacing.

Flagship Engine Boost: The flagship gains the boost-ability. Hold Left Shift to trigger a massive engine power surge with a charge bar, cooldown, and cost: weapons lock during the boost and rotation speed is reduced. This lets you use any ship design, not just hit-and-run specialists.

Full Config Exposure: Key balance-related values are tunable. Open the YAML file in the mod root and adjust boon values.

Optional SystemScanner: Speeds up exploration of unknown systems on entry. Toggle it on in settings.json. Default: off.

Balance Pass: Extensive playtesting across mod combinations. Your actual balance depends on which mods and ships you're running.

extras.saveCompatibility: Do not use on existing saves. Start a new game.

summary.sentence: Strips Starsector combat down to a single flagship, using a momentum-based progression system for temporary power surges and permanent campaign boons.
summary.paragraph: Players fight alone with only their flagship deployed, building momentum through kills to unlock escalating temporary bonuses and an ultimate state. Campaign progression allows spending points on persistent boons across various categories, while a new engine boost ability provides tactical repositioning options. The mod includes configurable balance settings and optional exploration tools.
